Olga / Marissa — quick analysis after skimming the telemetry:

- Traffic shape: strong diurnal with 30m microbursts (spikes up to 3.8–4.5k concurrent) and long tails from summary generation. The telemetry shows KV-cache reuse rate ~62% for multi-turn sessions (that helps).
- Short prompts (<=256 tokens) are ~72% of calls; those are candidates for low-latency optimized instances. Long generations (>=1k tokens) are rare (~3% by volume) but consume disproportionate token compute.

Sizing intuition (very rough):
- Interactive daytime pool: target net concurrency capacity of 4,500 sessions to meet p99 bursts with buffer. If we use an A100-style instance (quantized to 4-bit with optimized kernels) we can approximate 220 concurrent short-session backends per GPU for the 2k context profile. That suggests ~21–23 GPUs for primary pool.
- Night batch pool: isolate to separate reserved nodes sized for throughput (not latency). If batch jobs run for 12 hours each and can be scheduled across 6 jobs, a transient pool of 12–16 GPUs (depending on model size) should be sufficient — can be preemptible if NeonAI accepts reduced SLAs for batches.
- Fallback policy: reserve an overflow buffer of 4 GPUs in a cheaper region or lower-tier instance to snap up short bursts beyond pool capacity.

Risks / clarifying items for final plan:
1) Model size and quantization tolerance (3-bit/4-bit) — will affect the per-GPU concurrency.
2) Average response token distribution for the p99 (1,200 token response) — need to know how many of those overlap with bursts.
3) Region split — we may need to mirror pools in us-west and us-east rather than cross-region route for latency-sensitive traffic.

I'll draft a preliminary workbook with several SKU mixes (A100-quant, A100-full-precision, mixed with cheaper T4-like instances for background work) and send upstream.

-marcus

Subject: Proposed mutual action plan & preliminary fleet map (NEON-4721)

Hi Kelly — thanks again for the telemetry. We've sketched a preliminary reserved fleet map and an initial mutual action plan for the next 6–8 weeks. Attaching the workbook (redwood_prelim_sizing.xlsx) with three SKU mixes and a conservative plan that meets your p99 latency target while keeping a clear cost/buffer tradeoff. High-level proposal below: 

1) Daytime interactive reserved pool
- Primary: 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs (4-bit quantized stack) distributed across us-west and us-east (16 / 8 split) to keep p99 tail low by region. Estimated steady-state 1,300 active sessions with headroom for 4.5k concurrent bursts.
- Overflow: 4 smaller GPUs in a cross-region overflow cluster (lower-cost SKUs) to absorb extreme bursts with graceful degradation on long-generation requests.

2) Night batch pool
- Dedicated 14 x mid-tier GPUs isolated from interactive pool (can be scheduled or preemptible depending on preference). Jobs are CPU+GPU heavy but latency tolerant; we'll put them on cheaper SKUs if NeonAI accepts non-production SLAs for batch windows.

3) Routing & fallback
- Smart routing by request shape: short prompts routed to optimized low-latency queue; long generations routed to a separate execution lane that favors throughput. Automatic fallback to overflow cluster when regional queue saturates.

4) Next steps / asks from NeonAI
- Confirm model family / sizes and quantization tolerances (3/4-bit acceptable?).
- Provide histogram of long-generation overlap with burst windows (how often do the 1,200 token responses occur during the 30m microburst?).
- Approve draft MOP for night-batch isolation vs. shared pool.
